name: id
description: Prints the real and effective user and group IDs of the current user or a specified user.

flags.description: Your own UID, GID, and group memberships.
Print names instead of numbers (combine: id -nG).

examples.explanation: Shows your numeric IDs and every group you belong to — sudo and docker membership are visible here.
Checks another user's identity and groups without logging in as her.
Lists only the group names — handy in scripts: id -nG | grep -qw sudo.

about: id resolves names from /etc/passwd and /etc/group. The distinction between real and effective IDs matters for setuid programs; id shows both when they differ.
useCases: Check UID/GID values when fixing file ownership.
mistakes: Testing group changes without re-logging-in — id in an existing session still shows old groups.
